rationale: Fresh examination of the complete supplied EO 7431 text (characters 0-1475) and EO 7704 text (0-1488), independently of the prior blind verdict, supports this exact claim on its expressly provisional basis. EO 7431 identifies George C. Havenner, liaison officer, Government Printing Office, and closes with number 7431 and the August 17, 1936 signing line. Its inventory contains a single coupled presidential command: exemption from section 204 and continuance in service until October 1, 1937. Both its recital and operative sentence give that calendar limit; the verified ending span 1276-1367 supports 1937-10-01, not the signing date. The quoted statutory retirement rule supplies authority and context, and the expected September retirement age is what the exemption addresses, not an earlier cessation condition. The text specifies no separate earlier death, separation, retirement, performance or discretionary termination condition, and the permitted evidence establishes no earlier terminating event. A calendar limit on this grant can end its legal authority without proof that Havenner actually served through the limit. EO 7704, signed September 10, 1937, names the same employee and EO 7431 and grants a further exemption until October 1, 1938. Its operative language is an independent further grant; it does not replace EO 7431's date, expressly revoke the earlier order or prove uninterrupted service. Thus it does not displace the original order's own first ending. No independent post-term command or express savings clause appears in the complete original. Any compensation or credit actually accrued would be consequences of service, whose occurrence and amount remain unproved, rather than continuing operative authority. The whole-order own-terms ending and terminated/no-operative-force status at the October 14, 2026 cutoff are supported within the supplied search coverage. No current-operative predicate is needed for this expired grant. The inclusive treatment of October 1 is retained as a disclosed interpretation, with the exclusive beginning-of-day alternative unresolved by the text. Neither alternative affects cutoff status. Discovery of the other planted error and the old blind verdict supplied no approval for this decision.
